textPlacement.assessment: Both contexts preserve optional touch, available comfort, immediate protection and calm before discussion or repair, keeping the later calm-place example separate.
Both contexts preserve a few related, kind limits suited to age and ability, with acknowledged changes and neutral-time revision.
Both contexts retain company and supported shared activity, ongoing toddler supervision and announced departures without requiring long independent play.
Both contexts retain specific action descriptions and adult delight while avoiding fixed labels and interruptions of concentration.
Both contexts preserve immediate prevention of harm, observation without certain motive claims and supported repair after calm.
Both contexts preserve calm before repair and adult modeling for young children, without requiring an apology or independent restitution.
Both contexts retain observing patterns, removing objects that could hurt and distinguishing outdoor throwing from soft indoor possibilities.
Both contexts retain short information, processing time and concrete showing without promising that a cue or humor will always work.
The new perspective preserves the around-three versus over-three source distinction, voluntary use and continued comfort, without turning the example into an under-three isolation procedure.
